body.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\), where \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) is present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Let \(e\) be the endpoint at \(u\) on \(uv\). Then
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq \mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\]
Thus, if \(u\notin Z_k\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}\); if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\). If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the empty graph \(B_0\) on \(A(\eta)\) and the directed-edge graph \(B_P\) of any simple \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) are admissible and give two common-basal graphical replacement specifications preserving \(A(\eta)\) and every regime skeleton and unshielded collider on the full domains \(U_j\). The former has an arrowhead and the latter a tail at \(e\). In this two-mark case,
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\]
Here \(u\in Z_k\) denotes direct targeting or indirect affectedness within \(A(\eta)\), not necessarily \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this intervention-created-edge bracket.
body.justification: The corrected theorem proves the faithful-model outer bracket, exact singleton cases, and two graphical specifications for the two-mark case.
body.gap: Two-mark equality needs both corresponding faithful realization fibers to be nonempty.
body.consumer: It distinguishes already identified fixed-\(A\) endpoints from ambiguity that remains only graphical until faithful promotion.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:exact\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}graphical\mbox{-}frontier}\),
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\tag{1}
\]
Discarding the middle term proves the required nonempty inclusion.  In either singleton case in the definition of \(\mathcal G_A\), a nonempty subset of that singleton equals it, so (1) gives the two asserted law-level identifications.

If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the same lemma proves that \(B_0\) and every simple-path graph \(B_P\) are admissible; their replacement specifications preserve \(A(\eta)\) and the complete graphical signature on every \(U_j\), and their marks at \(e\) are respectively \(\mathtt{arrow}\) and \(\mathtt{tail}\).  If both displayed realization fibers are nonempty, \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) promotes one member of each fiber, not the bare graphical specifications themselves, into \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  The two opposite marks then belong to \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\); (1) and the two-element definition of \(\mathcal G_A\) give the asserted equality.  The interpretation of \(Z_k\) follows from the indicator-neighbor identity, and the exclusion of retained adjacencies is certified by \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\). \(\square\)
